panels.description:
In a Node.js application, both "heap size" and "heap used" refer to aspects of the V8 JavaScript engine's memory management, specifically within the heap. The heap is a region of memory used for dynamic memory allocation, where objects and data structures whose size is not known at compile time are stored.

Heap Size (or heapTotal):
- This represents the total size of the memory heap that has been allocated and reserved by the V8 engine for the Node.js process.
- It indicates the total amount of memory available for storing JavaScript objects, variables, and functions that are dynamically created during the application's execution.
- This value can grow as the application requires more memory, up to a certain limit (which can be configured using flags like --max-old-space-size).

Heap Used (heapUsed):
- This represents the actual amount of memory currently being utilized within the allocated heap by the Node.js process.
- It indicates how much of the heapTotal is actively holding live JavaScript objects and data.
- The difference between heapTotal and heapUsed represents the free space available within the allocated heap.
panels.title: V8 Engine Heap Total vs Size

panels.description: When a system is running with maximum CPU utilization, the transmitting and receiving threads must all share the available CPU. This will cause data to be queued more frequently to cope with the lack of CPU. CPU Saturation may be measured as the length of a wait queue, or the time spent waiting on the queue.
panels.title: CPU Saturation and Max Core Usage
